title: Allow the power-saver profile to be activated temporarily at critical battery level
line: Advanced Power Settings has a new "Switch to Power Save profile" option that puts the system in Power Save while the battery is critical and unplugged.
explanation: At the critical battery level PowerDevil only offered a final action (sleep, hibernate, shut down or nothing); the power profile stayed whatever the Low Battery profile set, so there was no way to use the strongest power saving only for the last few percent. The change adds a checkbox under "At critical level" in Advanced Power Settings (shown only when power profiles are supported, off by default). When enabled, the daemon takes a power-profiles-daemon HoldProfile("power-saver") while the battery is at or below the critical level and not on AC, and releases it when AC is plugged in, the level is raised or the option is turned off; it re-takes the hold after re-applying a profile's configured power profile, since setting the profile drops holds.

commits.message:
daemon: optionally switch to Power Save at critical battery level

The critical battery level only had a final action, so the power profile
stayed the same until the battery ran out. Add an option to hold the
power-saver profile while the battery is critical and not charging.

BUG: 525875

media.caption: Master: battery at 4% (critical), the power profile stays on Balanced.
With the option on: at 4% the profile switches to Power Save, and the applet shows it was requested by Power Management because the battery level is critical.
Master: Advanced Power Settings only has the critical level action.
New "Switch to Power Save profile" checkbox under "At critical level".

review.text: Works and the media show it, but the design bolts raw power-profiles-daemon D-Bus calls (HoldProfile/ReleaseProfile, cookie bookkeeping, release-then-rehold around loadProfile) onto Core, while powerdevil already has a PowerProfile action that owns the ppd interface, sets the per-profile power profile and manages holds. Because the logic sits outside that action, Core has to work around the action dropping holds when it sets a profile, and it borrows the KCM's app id so the applet labels it 'Power Management'. Maintainers are likely to want this inside the PowerProfile action, and it is a new user-facing option (new strings, design still open in powerdevil issue #10).
changes: Move the critical-battery hold into daemon/actions/bundled/powerprofile.cpp (reuse m_powerProfilesInterface; have the action apply the hold after its own profile Set instead of Core releasing and re-taking it around loadProfile)
Drive it from Core only through a small call or signal for the 'critical and on battery' state, not from raw D-Bus messages in powerdevilcore.cpp
Use powerdevil's own application id for the hold, or check with maintainers that reusing kcm_powerdevilprofilesconfig is acceptable
